meta.title: Starter checkpoint
meta.description: Reconnect tone direction, greeting meaning, first words, and conversation order.

objectives.canDo: Reconnect sound, vocabulary, and dialogue knowledge from the starter route.
Recognize the third tone by its low turning pitch.
Recognize how 叫 connects a speaker with a name.
Choose a natural response to a first greeting.
Place a name introduction in a natural exchange.

steps.title: Bring the first three lessons together
steps.instruction: Each prompt revisits something you already practiced. Missed answers return to your review queue.
steps.body: Move from sound to meaning, then rebuild the order of a first meeting.

steps.title: Recognize the pitch turn
steps.instruction: Play the cue and identify its tone before moving on.

feedback.correct: The pitch dipped low before turning upward: third tone.
feedback.retry: Replay the sample and listen for the turn near the bottom.

steps.title: Use 叫 inside a sentence
steps.instruction: Recall what 叫 does in the greeting pattern.
steps.prompt: What does 叫 do in “我叫安娜”?

options.label: It asks for the other person's name.

feedback.correct: 叫 connects 我 with the name that follows.
feedback.retry: Return to the pattern 我 + 叫 + name.

steps.title: Choose the natural reply
steps.instruction: Use the greeting exchange you explored earlier.
steps.prompt: Lin Yue says “你好！我叫林月。” What is the best reply?

options.label: 你好，林月！我叫安娜。
options.supportingText: Nǐ hǎo, Lín Yuè! Wǒ jiào Ānnà.

feedback.correct: Anna returns the greeting and then gives her own name.
feedback.retry: A first meeting reply should greet back before introducing a name.

steps.title: Rebuild the meeting
steps.instruction: Drag the three moments into a natural conversation order.
steps.prompt: What happens first, next, and last?

feedback.correct: Greeting, name, then a warm closing forms the full exchange.
feedback.retry: Start with hello, introduce the name, and close with nice to meet you.

steps.title: Your starter foundation is connected
steps.instruction: Finish the checkpoint to complete the first route.
takeaways: You can distinguish a turning tone from a direct fall.
You can recognize the pattern 我叫 + name.
You can follow the order of a first greeting.
